title: Managed Inference: Data Segregation & Subprocessor Obligations (Draft)
content:
Purpose and scope:

This draft is a contract exhibit intended for inclusion in Managed Inference engagements (hosted, dedicated, and private). It focuses on two linked obligations that often cause negotiation friction with enterprise customers: (1) the technical and evidentiary commitments around logical data segregation and residual data handling; and (2) the obligations and controls we require of subprocessors (including cloud providers, GPU hosts, and third-party operators).

Summary (TL;DR):
- Redwood will maintain logical segregation of customer inference data in the managed inference environment and will not use customer data for model training or product improvement except as expressly permitted in a separate agreement.
- Redwood will flow down security and data handling obligations to subprocessors, perform onboarding assessments, and provide remediation evidence on request under NDA.
- For on-prem or VPC-private deployments, the exhibit clarifies responsibilities (customer-managed network and physical control vs Redwood-managed runtime) and evidence types.

Notes to reviewers: bracketed items [IN BRACKETS] are negotiable placeholders. Sections marked "(ops note)" are implementation-side guidance and should be removed before final customer delivery unless called out in contract.

1. Definitions
- "Customer Data": any input, prompt, document, or other data supplied by Customer to Redwood for the purpose of Model Inference, plus any inference outputs identified as Customer Data under the main agreement.
- "Residual Data": ephemeral artifacts (e.g., KV cache segments, transient logs, memory snapshots) that may contain fragments of Customer Data during processing.
- "Subprocessor": any third party engaged by Redwood to process Customer Data or provide infrastructure for inference.

2. Data Segregation Commitments
2.1 Logical Segregation
Redwood will design and operate inference environments to segregate Customer Data logically from other customers' data. Logical segregation includes (but is not limited to): namespace isolation, per-tenant encryption contexts (where supported), runtime tenancy controls, and KV cache partitioning.

(ops note: runtime implements per-customer KV namespaces and enforces eviction policies per route config)

2.2 Data Handling and Non-Training Use
Redwood will not use Customer Data to train, evaluate, or improve models used in production inference unless Customer provides prior written consent. This limitation includes transfer of Customer Data to internal model-training pipelines or external research collaborations.

2.3 Residual Data Minimization and Deletion
Redwood will minimize retention of Residual Data by applying ephemeral storage primitives and by routinely expiring cached artifacts. Redwood will: 
- configure KV caches with per-tenant eviction and TTLs,
- scrub transient logs of Customer Data where safe to do so (see limitations below), and
- expose an API and audit log for Customer requests to trigger targeted cache eviction for active routing keys.

2.4 Limitations and Customer Responsibilities
Customer acknowledges that: 
- Certain low-level runtime artifacts may be inaccessible for targeted scrubbing without planned maintenance windows (e.g., GPU memory snapshots during preemptible events);
- In dedicated hardware scenarios where Customer elects to share physical hosts across business units, complete physical isolation may not be attainable;
- For on-prem deployments, Redwood cannot directly access physical storage for deletion-proof obligations; evidentiary flows are handled via HSM/KMS receipts and customer attestations.

3. Subprocessor Obligations
3.1 Flow-Down Requirements
Redwood will require subprocessors to implement materially equivalent data protection obligations as Redwood's commitments under the Main Agreement, including: data minimization, encryption in transit and at rest, access logging, personnel security screening, and breach notification timelines.

3.2 Onboarding and Continuous Assurance
Redwood will: 
- perform a documented onboarding assessment prior to adding a subprocessor;
- maintain a register of active subprocessors (provided to Customer quarterly on request under NDA);
- require subprocessors to provide attestation artifacts (SOC2, ISO27001, audit reports) and remediate identified gaps within commercially reasonable timelines.

3.3 Emergency Sequestration and Remediation Rights
In the event Redwood determines a subprocessor poses an unacceptable risk (vulnerability, legal restriction, or operational failure), Redwood will: 
- suspend data flows to the affected subprocessor where feasible;
- implement alternative processing routes and notify Customer within the breach-notification window; and
- provide a remediation plan and timeline.

(ops note: playbook reference -> linked_artifacts JIRA-SEC-842)

4. Evidence and Audit Access
4.1 Routine Evidence
Upon Customer request and execution of an NDA (where required), Redwood will provide: 
- attested architecture diagrams showing logical segregation for Customer routes;
- subprocessor register and recent attestations;
- redacted operational logs demonstrating cache eviction activity (range-limited to avoid revealing other customers' telemetry).

4.2 Onsite/Remote Audit Scope
If Customer requires a formal audit, the parties will follow the audit playbook in Exhibit X. Redwood will use reasonable efforts to support remote evidence collection and will coordinate onsite activities at mutually agreed times. Redwood reserves the right to redact proprietary tooling details and third-party confidential information.

5. Security Incidents and Notification
Redwood will follow the incident response obligations in the Main Agreement. For incidents involving a subprocessor, Redwood will include: summary of root cause, impacted Customer Data classes, mitigation steps taken, and steps to prevent recurrence.

6. Liability and Remedy (negotiable)
Parties may negotiate carve-outs and caps specific to failures of subprocessors or residual-data exposures. For on-prem and customer-controlled networks, Redwood's liability for physical or network-level failures shall be limited to Redwood-managed components.

7. Change Management and Model Variant Fallbacks
Redwood will: 
- notify Customer in advance of materially disruptive infra changes (e.g., model fork or runtime migration) that may affect segregation guarantees;
- provide fallback routing to compatible model variants if a subprocessor is decommissioned.

8. Customer Controls and Configuration Options
Redwood will provide configuration options to tighten segregation at increased cost: 
- dedicated GPU pools per customer (Reserved Capacity),
- increased TTL/eviction aggressiveness,
- no-logging routing mode (best-effort; may impact observability).

Pricing/ops note: these are premium options; product should feed into sales quoting templates.

9. Open Items / Negotiation Points (for internal negotiation with Sales/Legal)
- Whether Redwood will commit to per-customer key separation (KMS namespaces) by default or as paid option.
- Specific remediation SLA for subprocessor deficiencies (propose 30/90 day windows depending on severity).
- Exact form of evidence (raw logs vs. curated attestations) we are willing to hand to customers — coordinate with Product and Infra for practical export formats.
